claim: The authored doc line asserts that a flat `[[rls]]` rule whose `value_from_metadata` names a key other than the three identity keys blocks every verify case that reads its table, that identity values reach flat row-level security as the command-line strings, and that a passing run prints no account.
source_excerpt: - **`sqllens verify-memory` checks one identity per run.** The golden file has no per-case identity, and the command has no option for other `_meta` fields, so a flat `[[rls]]` rule whose `value_from_metadata` names another key blocks every case that reads its table. A run that passes its checks does not print the account it used, so after the file's only bound account changes, a command that omits `--account` runs under the new one without notice.
